proposals.before: Yu Wenhuaji appointed him administrator of Liyang, but he refused the post.
proposals.after: Yuwen Huaji appointed him administrator of Liyang, but he refused the post.
proposals.reason: 宇文 is the compound Xianbei surname Yuwen; writing "Yu Wenhuaji" splits the surname and obscures the person.

proposals.before: Yu Wen Huaji made him Administrator of Liyang but he did not accept.
proposals.after: Yuwen Huaji made him Administrator of Liyang but he did not accept.
proposals.reason: 宇文 is one surname; the literal spacing as three tokens is a romanization error.

proposals.before: Earlier, when Fu Gongshi rebelled, he forged orders in Fuwei's name to deceive the troops. After the Prince of Zhao Li Xiaogong had pacified Gongshi, he obtained the rebel correspondence and reported it to the throne.
proposals.after: Earlier, when Fu Gongshi rebelled, he forged orders in Fuwei's name to deceive the troops. After Li Xiaogong, Prince of Zhao Commandery, had pacified Gongshi, he obtained the rebel correspondence and reported it to the throne.
proposals.reason: 趙郡王 is Prince of Zhao Commandery, not the distinct title Prince of Zhao.

proposals.before: Wen Suian, a bandit of Suzhou, held Kunshan and acknowledged no master. Fuwei sent Wang Xiongdan against him. The stronghold was steep and well defended, and the siege dragged on for days. Wang Xiongdan then rode alone to the camp gate, proclaimed the majesty of the state, and laid out the consequences of resistance and submission. Wen Suian surrendered at once.
proposals.after: Wenren Suian, a bandit of Suzhou, held Kunshan and acknowledged no master. Fuwei sent Wang Xiongdan against him. The stronghold was steep and well defended, and the siege dragged on for days. Wang Xiongdan then rode alone to the camp gate, proclaimed the majesty of the state, and laid out the consequences of resistance and submission. Wenren Suian surrendered at once.
proposals.reason: 聞人 is the compound surname Wenren; "Wen Suian" drops 人 and misidentifies the name.

proposals.before: Suzhou bandit Wen Suian held Kunshan belonging to no one; Fuwei sent to attack; Xiongdan found the town steep and complete; attack drew out days; he alone rode to the camp gate, declared state prestige, opened persuasion of fortune and disaster; Suian at once submitted.
proposals.after: Suzhou bandit Wenren Suian held Kunshan belonging to no one; Fuwei sent to attack; Xiongdan found the town steep and complete; attack drew out days; he alone rode to the camp gate, declared state prestige, opened persuasion of fortune and disaster; Suian at once submitted.
proposals.reason: 聞人 is the compound surname Wenren, not the monosyllable Wen.

proposals.before: Wang Xiongdan was by nature upright and trusting, and he believed the story. He returned to quarters and feigned illness.
proposals.after: Wang Xiongdan was by nature upright and trusting, and he believed the story. He returned to quarters and took to his sickbed.
proposals.reason: 臥疾 means he took to his sickbed; the Chinese does not say the illness was feigned.

proposals.before: In the first year of Wude he pledged allegiance and was appointed commander of Ling Prefecture and Duke of Jinhe, then re-enfeoffed as Duke of Bie.
proposals.after: In the first year of Wude he pledged allegiance and was appointed commander of Ling Prefecture and Duke of Jinhe, then re-enfeoffed as Duke of Cheng.
proposals.reason: 郕國公 is Duke of Cheng (郕); Bie is a misreading of the place-name.

proposals.before: In the first year of Wude he submitted allegiance; he was appointed Chief Commander of Ling Prefecture and Duke of Jinhe Commandery, then transferred to Duke of Bie.
proposals.after: In the first year of Wude he submitted allegiance; he was appointed Chief Commander of Ling Prefecture and Duke of Jinhe Commandery, then transferred to Duke of Cheng.

proposals.before: South of Taiyuan are many cliff barriers; now bundling armor deep inward with no following army—loss cannot be repaid—better join Turks with Tang in alliance, style oneself king on the south, supreme stratagem."
proposals.after: South of Taiyuan are many cliff barriers; now bundling armor deep inward with no following army—loss cannot be repaid—better ally with the Turks against Tang and style oneself king on the south, supreme stratagem."
proposals.reason: 連突厥與唐合從 advises allying with the Turks, not forming an alliance that includes Tang.

proposals.before: When Yu Wenhuaji reached Shandong he sent envoys to win Luo Yi over. Luo Yi replied, "I am a loyal servant of the Sui. The dynasty lies in ruins—I will not endure insult from a rebel."
proposals.after: When Yuwen Huaji reached Shandong he sent envoys to win Luo Yi over. Luo Yi replied, "I am a loyal servant of the Sui. The dynasty lies in ruins—I will not endure insult from a rebel."
proposals.reason: 宇文 is the compound surname Yuwen.

proposals.before: When Yu Wen Huaji reached Shandong he sent envoys to recruit Yi; Yi said: "I am an old minister of Sui; now the Great Line is overturned—I will not suffer disgrace from bandits."
proposals.after: When Yuwen Huaji reached Shandong he sent envoys to recruit Yi; Yi said: "I am an old minister of Sui; now the Great Line is overturned—I will not suffer disgrace from bandits."
proposals.reason: 宇文 is one surname, not three tokens.

proposals.before: When Emperor Taizong took the throne, Luo Yi was promoted to Grand Master of Splendor with Golden Seal and Purple Girdle.
proposals.after: When Emperor Taizong took the throne, Luo Yi was promoted to Commander Unequalled in Honor.
proposals.reason: 開府儀同三司 is Kaifu Yitong Sansi, not 金紫光祿大夫 (Grand Master of Splendor with Golden Seal and Purple Girdle).

proposals.before: When Taizong ascended he was advanced to Grand Master of Splendor with Golden Seal and Purple Girdle.
proposals.after: When Taizong ascended he was advanced to Commander Unequalled in Honor (kaifu yitong sansi).
proposals.reason: The literal also mistranslates 開府儀同三司 as a different honorific.

proposals.before: He separately reduced Xuanyuan and Luochuan counties, defeated Wang Shichong's general Wei Yin, struck the grain route at Jian, and sank thirty supply barges.
proposals.after: He separately reduced Xuanyuan and Luochuan counties, defeated Wang Shichong's general Wei Yin, struck the grain route at Goushi, and sank thirty supply barges.
proposals.reason: 緱氏 is Goushi, not Jian.

proposals.before: He entered alone and said urgently, "There is an emergency—I must report it!" Wang Chen was bathing. Wang Junguo seized him by the hair as he came out and cut off his head, then took Li Yuan prisoner.
proposals.after: Wang Chen was bathing. He came out grasping his hair; Wang Junguo beheaded him at once and then seized Li Yuan.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic sentence duplicates s0187's speech and misassigns who grasped the hair; the Chinese is 詵方沐，握發出，即斬之，因執瑗.

decisions.reason: 宇文 is the compound surname Yuwen and must not be split from Huaji's given name.
The literal field contains the same erroneous split of the compound surname 宇文.
趙郡王 is specifically Prince of Zhao Commandery, not the separate title Prince of Zhao.
聞人 is the compound surname Wenren; the current English drops its second character.
The literal field likewise needs the full compound surname Wenren for 聞人.
臥疾 says that Xiongdan took to his sickbed; it does not characterize the illness as feigned.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 雄誕性質厚，信之，還臥疾

decisions.reason: 郕 is the place-name Cheng; Bie is a character misreading.
The literal field contains the same misreading of 郕 as Bie instead of Cheng.
The proposal correctly resolves the intended strategy as joining the Turks in opposition to Tang.
宇文 is Yuwen, a compound surname, in the idiomatic field as well.
The literal field should preserve the compound surname Yuwen without internal spaces.

decisions.after: When Emperor Taizong took the throne, Luo Yi was promoted to Kaifu Yitong Sansi.
decisions.reason: The worker correctly rejects the unrelated Grand Master title, but Commander Unequalled in Honor is not a reliable rendering of 開府儀同三司; the established corpus form is Kaifu Yitong Sansi.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 太宗即位，進開府儀同三司

decisions.after: When Taizong ascended he was advanced to Kaifu Yitong Sansi.
decisions.reason: The literal field should use the established transliteration of 開府儀同三司 rather than substitute another honorific.
緱氏 is the locality Goushi, not Jian.

decisions.after: Wang Shen was bathing. He came out holding up his hair; Wang Junguo beheaded him at once and then seized Li Yuan.
decisions.reason: The worker identifies both defects, but the replacement should name Wang Shen correctly and make clear that the bathing man, not Junguo, emerged holding his hair.
